doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Staying in New York: Monk at the Five Spot and the Open Door with Bird
summary: He took local jobs with Kenny Burrell and Monk, and recalls the 1954 Bird group with Monk and Mingus and Mingus's scene on Bud Powell's gig.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: So in order to facilitate your family life, you would just take gigs here in the New York area? You would minimize your touring?
Yes. I had been around a lot. Yeah. That’s when I started doing things with Kenny Burrell a little bit then. The Vanguard – I think we did a record down there. And the Monk thing . . .
. . . which was a low-paying thing, too.
The Five Spot. But that’s starting to get . . .
It was a lot of fun, and it was a challenge.
Is that the first time you’d played with Monk? No, because you played with him in ’54, because the picture at the – the famous picture with you, Mingus, Monk, Bird.
Right. Well, he was a sideman then. We were playing . . .
Bird was the leader of that group?
If I remember correctly, because – what’s the guy? Bob Reisner. Yeah, that was Bird’s thing.
That must have been interesting to have Mingus and Monk and you and Bird in the group. What was the dynamic between Monk and Bird?

I don’t even remember that. I don’t remember. I think – I don’t know if we did a complete week there. We might have done a weekend. I don’t remember exactly. I don’t remember. But I also did some other things with Mingus and Bud [Powell] that was Bud’s gig, so it wasn’t the Mingus that we – even though Mingus went out a little bit while he was there. He went out.
On Bud’s gig? Yeah, that’s the famous – Mingus storming out.

Yeah, he didn’t go out necessary on. Backstage there was some scenes where – there was some scenes. He was going through different things backstage that ended up seeming like he was the one that was just let out of the hospital and that Bud was the cool one.
